host.evidence_quote: Canines were the most common animal host (138/204, 67.6%), followed by equine (25/204, 12.3%), feline (17/204, 8.3%), other mammals (10/204, 4.9%), avian (6/204, 2.9%), bovine (5/204, 2.5%), and porcine (3/204, 1.5%).

collection_date.evidence_quote: Isolates were collected from 26 states by a network of 30 Vet-LIRN veterinary diagnostic laboratories ("Source laboratories") from January 2019 to December 2020.

notes: SIZING: ENA records 630 Klebsiella samples and 1559 total samples for this accession. The paper describes only 204/630 Klebsiella (32.4% coverage), consistent with Pattern C (shared/umbrella accession). The EBI description 'Historical Archived Isolates' confirms this is a broad Vet-LIRN collection extending beyond the 2019–2020 paper cohort. STUDY SETTING: All isolates are non-human veterinary patients; per rubric, non-human hosts at veterinary hospitals/diagnostic labs = community. The EBI description ('Veterinary Pathogens') supports this for the whole project, making it gradeable. AMR_STUDY: The paper's 204 isolates were surveillance-selected (one Klebsiella per client submission from sick animals, no AMR gate; AMR characterised post hoc). However, paper coverage is only 32%, and the EBI description does not explicitly state the sampling rule for the broader accession, so graded partial. No AMR selection gate is apparent; no carbapenem resistance genes were identified. COHORT_AGE: Non-human animal hosts; human age-band categories are not applicable. BACKFILL: Country=USA is gradeable for the whole project as Vet-LIRN is an explicit US FDA program. Isolation source and host are not constant across the project (multiple body systems and animal species). Collection date cannot be backfilled for the whole project because the EBI description references 'Historical Archived Isolates' of uncertain temporal span beyond the paper's 2019–2020 window, and coverage is only 32%.

notes: KEY DISCREPANCY: The paper explicitly states its sequencing data were deposited under PRJEB29738, not PRJEB17615. PRJEB17615 is the parent 'See and Sequence' Philippines programme (1284 total samples, 365 K. pneumoniae), while PRJEB29738 is a component/child study. The paper's 259 Klebsiella isolates (all AMR-selected: ESBL/cephalosporin/carbapenem resistant) cover at most 71% of PRJEB17615's 365 K. pneumoniae — below the 75% threshold. Study-level attributes graded 'gradeable' rely on the EBI description for PRJEB17615 itself: the description explicitly states 'susceptible and resistant isolates' (supporting amr_study=mixed) and describes a human hospital-based clinical surveillance program (supporting study_setting=hospital). amr_target (multiple resistance types: ESBL/3GC + carbapenem = other) and amr_method (ast_result: all selection criteria are phenotypic) are graded 'partial' because the paper is formally about a different accession and paper coverage for PRJEB17615 is below 75%. Collection period 2015–2017 spans >2 years, so collection_date backfill is not applied.
